text:
maria: Heads-up 1: OrionCompute asked to validate perf/W for their latest board before we put a joint blog post out. They want a short acceptance checklist we can both sign.

dina: Good. Let's make the gate narrow but measurable. Suggested items: steady-state perf/W, thermal headroom (no throttles), and reproducibility across runs and racks.

noah: Agreed. Also require a short methods note: ambient, distro/driver versions, kernel flags, and quantization path (fp16 vs int8) used. Partners often forget driver pins.

maria: Draft gate: 
- Hardware: Orion X1 8x card chassis, airflow medium, inlet 23C +-2C
- Software: OS ubuntu-22.04, nvidia-driver 535.x, rwd-runtime v2.4.1, model: rwd-7b-quant (fp16 and int8)
- Workload: 512-token prompts, 16 concurrent clients, 20 minute steady-state window after warmup
- Metrics: seq/s (avg), 95/99 latency, wall power (W), perf/W = seq/s / avg_power(W)
- Stability: 3 independent runs across 2 racks (total 6 runs); throughput coeff var <4%

sam: Add thermal headroom clause: no throttle events in dmesg and package temps <85C on cards. If any card hits throttle, fail and provide thermal logs.

noah: For reproducibility, require artifact bundle from partner: a) condensed perf logs b) a small anonymized KV snippet for one run c) dockerfile + pins for runtime. We'll host on s3 for cross-check.

dina: For passing thresholds, propose two paths: 
- Baseline parity: perf/W within 7% of Redwood ref on same model and config OR
- Throughput-first: throughput >= 95% of baseline while keeping 95th latency within baseline + 20ms and no thermal events.

maria: That gives flexibility. Also call out acceptable mitigations: if power budget exceeded, we allow power-capping to meet perf/W but only if throughput loss <8% and partner documents changes.

bench-bot: created validation job: rwd-orion-1788, schedule: 2026-08-03T14:00Z. Artifacts will post to #partnerships-results and s3://redwood-partner-artifacts/rwd-orion-1788/

noah: One more: require a short quote from Orion engineering confirming the driver/kernel flags used for the run for the methods appendix. No marketing claims until both parties sign.

sam: I'll prep a tiny capture script for synchronized power+throughput sampling. Suggest 10s sample interval and include UTC timestamps. Example snippet: 
```bash
for i in $(seq 1 120); do
  ts=$(date -u +%s)
  pwr=$(ipmi-sensor-cli read PWR | awk '{print $2}')
  tput=$(curl -s http://localhost:9100/metrics | grep \"rwd_seq_per_s\" | awk '{print $2}')
  echo \"$ts,$pwr,$tput\" >> orion-run.csv
  sleep 10
done
```

dina: Perfect. For public release: we'll only publish aggregated perf/W numbers and a one-paragraph methods note. Raw logs remain partner-only.

maria: OK I'll turn this into a one-pager to send to Orion eng and legal. Plan: run, validate, then legal/PR signoff. Who owns follow-ups? @noah on artifacts ingestion, @sam on capture scripts, @dina on methods appendix, I'll handle partner comms.

maria: Thanks team. Closing thread until results are in. Will reopen with job link and initial numbers. :white_check_mark:
